chapter: Coleman Hawkins, Bernie Young and doubling on tenor
title: The 1923 Bernie Young recording and Stump Evans's C-melody
summary: Personnel of the 1923 record; Stump Evans, from Kansas City, played C-melody, which people mistook for alto, and Hawkins asked about him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, when you -- just back to that record. You did record (unintelligible) in '23. with Bernie Young (unintelligible) then) (unintelligible)
'23. First I (unintelligible) we started with because we skipped (unintelligible), but Bernie Young on Mike McKendrick trumpet, Mack Hendricks on guitar, Preston Jackson on trombone.
Casino? [Cassino]
I played clarinet. He went to New Orleans last year to live.
Who?
Preston Jackson did.
Oh, yeah?

He got a lot of work there. That's his home, you know. But he was raised up in Chicago. And Stump Evans. See, Stump was a trombone player and a saxophone player. He was from out of St. Joe -- out of Kansas City, Missouri.
But what instrument -- what was he playing, alto or tenor?
He was playing alto. No, he was playing, c- melody.
Oh.
Or that (Unintelligible) recording. I played on the -- strictly clarinet.
Yeah.

But a lot of people didn't know that Stump -- even Hawk didn't know it, until Hawk -- until I ran into Hawk one day up there in the Masonic temple, and he said to me, he said, Hap, I want to ask you a question. I said, what you want, Bean? I said, anything. I never heard Stump, but I heard him, you know, from records, said, what kind of fellow was he? I said, Hawk, if he'd come here like we do anything, you know, that you asked him to, said, he'd upset everybody like you did. He said, well, what else did he play? I said, trombone and c-melody (Unintelligible).
Yeah. But then he went to tenor.
Then he went to tenor. When we sent for him to come to New York, Cab wanted to --
You know, think it was Earl Hines told me that when -- (at the Sunset) -- he was in that band?
Yeah.
Well, he said, you know, he kept telling -- great tenor player! I said, no, the man played -- I thought he played the alto. No, he said, tenor.
Well, he -- a lot of people might think (unintelligible) trombone. 'cause his horn was C-melody and
Yeah.
But on this recording we made with Bernie, you know, he's on (unintelligible) C-melody.
Yeah. Yeah. Lots of people would think that's an alto.
Yes, well, they would. It's the tone, you know, so similar. I used to play (unintelligible) C-melody, and Benny Carter did too.
